text:
ana (PM): quick thread — need alignment on how we prioritize the rate-limit / packaging work. Two options on the table:
- A: soft rate limits + UX for auto-upgrade (lower lift, incremental revenue).
- B: formal tiered limits + reserved capacity product with SLA (bigger lift, predictable recurring revenue).
I want to use a prioritization framework (RICE or impact/effort) and sequence experiments. Inputs pls.

chris (Eng): eng perspective — soft limits are the fastest path. We can ship enforcement + notification + grace windows as a 2-sprint spike for MVP.
Reserved product is non-trivial: needs billing integration, scheduler for capacity, autoscaling rules, and can be ~8-10 sprints to ship properly. Per-route quotas add more complexity.

priya (Sales): fyi from field — 3 pilot customers explicitly asked for reserved capacity + an SLA this quarter. They'll only sign enterprise deals with commitment and clear SLOs. Soft limits are fine for startup customers but won't close those deals.

jordan (Finance): finance lens — reserved gives higher committed ARR but higher build + opex. For prioritization use RICE: Reach (number of customers affected), Impact (revenue uplift / churn reduction), Confidence, Effort. If Sales can surface ARR estimates for the 3 pilots we can model payback.

viktor (Data): we can run a quick analysis on request distributions. Early numbers: last 6 months shows 70% requests under 2k tokens, but 5% of tenants cause 40% of peak tokens. Smart caching + soft limits could reduce required reserved headroom by ~25-35%.

chris (Eng): follow-ups/questions: do we treat quotas org-level or per-route? Enterprise wants per-route guarantees sometimes (e.g., embeddings throughput). Per-route = more state and harder autoscaling. Also need to decide if soft limits are push-notice-only or block requests after grace.

priya (Sales): for pilots they'll accept org-level reserved first if time is limited, then we can productize per-route in a follow-up. Main ask is deterministic latency/throughput during peak windows.

ana (PM typing) — typo correction: ana (PM) :)

deploy-bot: deploy created for spike: feature/soft-quota (branch), env=staging.

ana (PM): suggested next steps:
1) Run a 2-week spike to implement soft limits + telemetry to measure blocked vs retried requests (owner: chris).
2) Sales to collect ARR & commitment likelihood for the 3 pilots (owner: priya).
3) Data to produce a headroom model and percent reduction from caching (owner: viktor).
4) Finance to run payback sensitivity (owner: jordan).
5) Schedule a 90-minute RICE workshop next Wed to score A vs B and decide sequencing.

Decision ask: can devs start the spike next sprint and Sales confirm pilot ARR by EOW?@chris @priya

chris (Eng): we can start spike next sprint, allocate 1 eng + 0.5 infra SRE.

priya (Sales): I'll get preliminary ARR numbers by Fri and sync with pilots.

jordan (Finance): will prep a simple revenue/op cost template for the workshop.

ana (PM): great — outcome for the workshop: clear RICE scores, recommended sequence (soft limits first + telemetry, reserved product follow if pilots validate), and launch criteria for reserved (min committed ARR, SLO definitions, resource playbook).

chris (Eng): one more engineering constraint — if we go reserved later we should design the soft-limit spike so it doesn't block future reserved architecture (avoid hard-coupling to single quota store).

ana (PM): noted. will add that to spike acceptance criteria. thanks all :thumbsup:
